business_process: Physical access control and credentialing
description: Door and turnstile access for about 212,000 credential holders; issuing and revoking cards and mobile credentials; door schedules and after-hours access at 140 properties
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Doors must lock and unlock on schedule. Door controllers cache credentials for up to 72 hours, but no credential can be issued or revoked while the cloud platform or a property network is down; a revoked credential that still works is a physical security exposure. Officers can staff about 900 main entrances for one shift before overtime and fatigue limits are reached. RPO 1 hour matches the rate of credential changes (about 1,900 per business day)
manual_workaround: Officers post at main entrances with printed tenant lists; perimeter doors set to scheduled lock; turnstiles to card-only; credential changes queued on paper and entered on recovery
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-09 (console PCs); SYS-14 (mobile credentials)
dependent_third_parties: Access control and video platform vendor; 3 regional access control and video integrators; SD-WAN provider; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vice President, Corporate Security; RSOC operators; 4,900 security staff; lobby desks at 70 properties
quantified_impact_basis: Officer overtime to post about 900 entrances (about $490,000), temporary credentials and tenant service credits (about $160,000)
acquired_portfolio_dependency: 19 acquired properties run the legacy PACS (2 on-premises servers, no tested backup)
single_points_of_failure: Enterprise access control platform (one vendor, 121 properties)

business_process: Regional Security Operations Center (RSOC) monitoring, alarm response, and video
description: Live monitoring of about 43,900 cameras, door alarms, and BAS critical alarms from 3 RSOCs; incident dispatch; video requests from police, insurers, and tenants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The RSOCs are the only place that sees each region as a whole. Without them, door-forced alarms and BAS critical alarms go unanswered and officers are dispatched by radio only. Each RSOC can take over another region, but regional failover has been tested for 4 hours only. Video is recorded locally on NVRs, so RPO applies to platform configuration (24 hours)
manual_workaround: Officers on increased patrols; property desks watch local NVR clients; radio dispatch; BAS critical alarms phoned to chief engineers; another RSOC takes over the region
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-09 (RSOC console PCs)
dependent_third_parties: Access control and video platform vendor; access control and video integrators; guard contractors
dependent_people_or_facilities: RSOC operators (3 centers, 24x7); security officers; RSOC facilities in Florida, Texas, and California
quantified_impact_basis: Patrol overtime and guard contractor surge staffing across 3 regions
acquired_portfolio_dependency: Acquired properties use a legacy video system monitored by property desks only
single_points_of_failure: RSOC regional failover tested for 4 hours only

business_process: Tenant emergency and service communications
description: Building notices, weather and emergency instructions, and service interruption notices to about 5,600 tenant contacts and occupants by tenant app push, SMS, email, and phone tree
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: During any building systems outage or hurricane event, occupants must get instructions within hours. In-building emergency voice systems are separate (SYS-13), but occupant-wide notices outside an alarm event depend on the tenant app and email. Lease clauses require prompt notice of service interruptions; about 1,100 leases have 72-hour notice clauses for data incidents
manual_workaround: Phone tree to tenant contacts from printed lists kept at each property; lobby signage; floor wardens; text messages from Property Managers company phones
dependent_third_parties: SMS and messaging provider; productivity suite vendor; mobile carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Executive Vice President, Property Operations; Property Managers; Vice President, Corporate Communications
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time for manual notification and tenant service credits; reputational effects not quantified
acquired_portfolio_dependency: Acquired properties are not yet on the tenant app; notices go by email only
single_points_of_failure: One SMS and messaging provider for push and text notices

business_process: Building environmental control on BAS Platform A
description: Supervisory control and alarm handling for chillers, cooling towers, air handlers, VAV boxes, lighting schedules, and meters at 50 office towers and 14 mixed-use properties
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Field controllers keep their last programs, but nobody can change setpoints, answer chiller or air handler alarms, or run after-hours HVAC. Tower floors and tenant data rooms overheat within one business day in the southern and southwestern climates. Manual rounds on 20 to 60 floors need every engineer on site; crews tire after about 12 hours. Office leases on the 2023 template allow rent abatement after 3 consecutive business days. RPO 4 hours matches the rate of program and schedule changes across 64 properties
manual_workaround: Chief engineers switch plant equipment to local hand control and run hourly rounds; portable cooling for tenant data rooms; lighting on local switches; after-hours HVAC by request to the engineer on duty
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (Platform A clusters in DC-1 and DC-2); SYS-04; SYS-08 (data platform, backups, OT remote access gateway); SYS-09 (engineering workstations and tablets)
dependent_third_parties: BAS Integrator A; colocation providers; equipment service contractors; portable cooling rental vendors; energy optimization vendor (AI-004)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Senior Vice President, Engineering; Building Technology Directors; chief engineers and about 2,100 engineering staff at Platform A properties
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering overtime and manual rounds (about $260,000), portable cooling for tenant data rooms (about $190,000), lost after-hours HVAC and event revenue (about $70,000)
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None (acquired towers are on Platform C)
single_points_of_failure: None at platform level (clusters fail over between DC-1 and DC-2); the 4 clusters share one Active Directory forest for OT

business_process: Building environmental control on BAS Platform B
description: Supervisory control for rooftop units, air handlers, parking and site lighting, and meters at 21 office parks and 36 retail centers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rooftop units run on local schedules and most retail tenants control their own space temperature. Site and parking lot lighting schedules are on the BAS and matter for evening safety. Retail leases allow abatement after 5 business days, office park leases after 3. A sampled restore of a Platform B site server took 14 hours in 2026, against the 12-hour RTO
manual_workaround: Local hand control of rooftop units; site lighting on photocell override; engineers on extended rounds; guard patrols in parking fields after dark
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (Platform B, 57 site servers); SYS-04; SYS-08 (backup accounts); SYS-09 (engineering tablets)
dependent_third_parties: BAS Integrators B1 to B4; HVAC service contractors; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Regional engineering directors; chief engineers and about 1,000 engineering staff at Platform B properties
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering overtime, rooftop unit service calls, and guard patrols for unlit parking fields
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None
single_points_of_failure: Integrator B3 holds the only copies of controller programs for 9 properties

business_process: Building operations at the acquired portfolio (Platform C and legacy PACS)
description: BAS supervisory control, door access, and video at the 19 properties acquired in November 2025 (AP-01 to AP-19) in Texas and Arizona
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same drivers as BP-04 and BP-01 for 19 properties, in hot climates. The 19 Platform C site servers have no backups and Integrator C holds the only copies of controller programs, so the 8-hour RTO is a target the company cannot meet today (gap 1). The legacy PACS cannot issue or revoke credentials if its servers are lost
manual_workaround: Local hand control; officers at entrances; legacy PACS controllers keep their cached credential lists; property desks watch local video clients
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (Platform C); SYS-02 (legacy PACS); SYS-03 (legacy video); SYS-04 (flat property networks); SYS-11 (legacy kiosks at 6 towers)
dependent_third_parties: BAS Integrator C; legacy PACS and video service vendor; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vice President, Integration Management Office; 19 chief engineers; about 380 engineering and security staff at the acquired properties
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering and security overtime and portable cooling at 19 properties
acquired_portfolio_dependency: All of it: Platform C, legacy PACS, legacy video, legacy kiosks, flat networks
single_points_of_failure: Platform C servers (no backups); Integrator C (sole holder of programs)

business_process: Visitor management
description: Registering visitors, scanning ID, printing passes, and turnstile passes at 70 lobbies (about 18,000 visitors per business day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Lobbies can run on paper logs with officers checking ID, but entry slows to about a third of normal speed and tenants complain within hours. Visitor ID scans are sensitive personal information for California visitors (Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140(ae)(1)(A))
manual_workaround: Paper visitor log; officer escort; tenants pre-register by email to the lobby desk
dependent_third_parties: Visitor management vendor; legacy kiosk vendor (6 acquired towers)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Lobby officers at 70 properties
quantified_impact_basis: Officer overtime for manual check-in and tenant service credits
acquired_portfolio_dependency: 6 acquired towers use a legacy kiosk product that keeps ID images beyond the standard (gap 8)

business_process: Tenant experience platform and mobile credentials
description: Mobile credentials, amenity bookings, building notices, service requests, and the virtual assistant for about 168,000 active users at company properties and about 41,000 at SL-2 client buildings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 92,000 tenant employees use only mobile credentials; if the app or its PACS integration fails, they need temporary cards at lobby desks, which cannot be printed fast enough at peak. SL-2 clients rely on the platform under service agreements (99.9% monthly availability). RPO 1 hour protects credential issuance records
manual_workaround: Temporary cards issued at lobby desks from the access control platform; notices by email (BP-03); service requests by phone
dependent_systems: SYS-14 (Cloud provider B, two regions); SYS-02; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; access control and video platform vendor (credential integration); SMS and messaging provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vice President, Digital Products; digital product engineering team; lobby officers
quantified_impact_basis: Temporary credentials and lobby overtime (about $180,000) and SL-2 service credits (about $80,000)
acquired_portfolio_dependency: Acquired properties are not yet on the platform
single_points_of_failure: Credential integration with one access control platform vendor

business_process: Engineering work orders and tenant service requests
description: Tenant requests, preventive maintenance, after-hours HVAC requests, and contractor dispatch (about 4,200 new requests per business day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Requests can be taken by phone for two days; preventive maintenance can slip a few days. Records support insurance and warranty claims
manual_workaround: Phone and email requests to each management office; paper work orders entered later
dependent_third_parties: Property management and ERP vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Engineering staff; tenant services coordinators
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time for manual intake and later data entry
acquired_portfolio_dependency: Acquired properties use the seller work order system until 2027-03

business_process: Third-party property management and building operations services (SL-1)
description: TRS services for 50 JV and third-party properties: operations, engineering, security, work order and service-level reporting, and submeter billing to owners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Owners receive monthly operating and service-level reports and submeter bills; management agreements set service levels and require notice of material incidents within 2 business days. Data must be accurate (processing integrity) because owners bill their tenants from it
manual_workaround: Reports built from system exports; owners told of delays in writing
dependent_systems: SYS-07; SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-08 (data platform and warehouse)
dependent_third_parties: Property management and ERP vendor; cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: TRS management team; property accountants
quantified_impact_basis: Management fee credits, owner reporting penalties, and staff time
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Rent billing, collections, and tenant accounting
description: Monthly rent and recovery invoices (about $370 million a month), ACH collection, receivables, and CAM reconciliation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most rent is collected in the first 5 business days of the month. A delay then moves cash, not revenue. The SaaS vendor holds its own backups; SOX controls depend on the system
manual_workaround: Invoice from the prior month register; tenants pay by bank transfer; credit facility
dependent_third_parties: Property management and ERP vendor; banks
dependent_people_or_facilities: Finance and accounting staff
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time and finance charges; up to about $310 million of cash delayed if the outage falls in the first week of a month
acquired_portfolio_dependency: Acquired properties billed from SYS-07 since 2026-02

business_process: Treasury, accounts payable, and debt service
description: Vendor payments (about 21,000 a month), payroll funding, debt service of about $95 million a month on fixed dates, and wires
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Missed debt service is a default event under loan agreements. Bank portals are separate from company systems, but payment files come from SYS-07. Business email compromise is a fraud risk during any outage
manual_workaround: Bank portal payments from clean laptops with dual approval; manual check run
dependent_third_parties: Banks; property management and ERP vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Treasurer; treasury and accounts payable staff
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time and late payment fees; debt service exposure is managed by paying through bank portals
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Financial close, SEC reporting, and REIT compliance
description: Monthly and quarterly close, Forms 10-Q and 10-K, REIT income and asset tests, and SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Close can slip a few days except at quarter end, when SEC filing deadlines cut the MTD to 48 hours. A late or wrong filing is a regulatory and reputational event
manual_workaround: Work from system exports and the last trial balance; ask for filing relief only with counsel
dependent_third_parties: Property management and ERP vendor; payroll vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Chief Accounting Officer; Controller; financial reporting team
quantified_impact_basis: Staff overtime; quarter-end exposure is regulatory rather than monetary
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Leasing and lease administration
description: Prospect tours, lease drafting, critical dates, and lease abstracts (AI-005)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No same-day dependency; lease critical dates are tracked monthly
manual_workaround: Work from signed lease copies in cloud file storage
dependent_third_parties: Property management and ERP vendor; lease abstraction AI vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Leasing team; lease administration
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time; missed critical dates only if the outage spans a deadline
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Payroll and HR
description: Time capture and biweekly payroll for 12,000 employees (about 8,600 hourly), onboarding, and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll is about $31 million per pay period; a missed payroll has legal and retention impact for hourly staff. Terminations feed identity governance (PS-4)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper timesheets; manual termination tickets to IT
dependent_third_parties: Payroll and HR vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Chief Human Resources Officer; payroll staff
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time and correction payments after recovery
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Card payment acceptance
description: Conference and event bookings, after-hours HVAC charges, badge replacement fees, and kiosk license fees at 64 offices (about 575 transactions a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers can pay by invoice or ACH
manual_workaround: Invoice the customer; take payment later on a working P2PE terminal (never on paper)
dependent_third_parties: Payment processor (P2PE solution provider)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Management office and conference center staff
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed collection and staff time
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Parking operations and revenue
description: Garage entry and exit, monthly permits, transient revenue, and license plate recognition (AI-003) at 84 garages run by 3 parking operators
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: If gates or the revenue system fail, operators raise the gates and parking is free; the company revenue share (about $300,000 a day) is lost for the period. Tenant parking ratios are lease obligations
manual_workaround: Gates up; operator staff verify monthly permits by sticker; cash-free exits counted for reconciliation
dependent_systems: Parking operator systems (outside company systems); SYS-04 (garage networks at 14 mixed-use properties)
dependent_third_parties: Parking operators (3)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Parking operator staff
quantified_impact_basis: Lost company share of parking revenue
acquired_portfolio_dependency: 4 acquired garages use the seller operator under a transition agreement

business_process: Energy management, submetering, and the smart building data platform
description: BAS historian, energy analytics, the AI energy optimization service (AI-004), and submetered utility billing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Optimization saves about 5% of tower energy cost; submeter bills are monthly
manual_workaround: Run the BAS on fixed schedules without optimization; estimate submeter bills from prior months
dependent_third_parties: Energy optimization vendor; cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Energy management team; chief engineers
quantified_impact_basis: Lost energy savings (about $40,000 a day) and staff time
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

description: Quarterly investor materials and monthly and quarterly reports to JV partners and lenders from the data warehouse
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadlines are about 15 business days after month end
manual_workaround: Reports built from SYS-07 exports
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A

quantified_impact_basis: Staff time
acquired_portfolio_dependency: None

business_process: Corporate collaboration and communications

mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most corporate work stops without email and files. Incident teams switch to the out-of-band conferencing service
manual_workaround: Company phones and the out-of-band conferencing service; local copies of key files
